page: Amazon Web Services c3.4xlarge is a third-generation compute-optimized virtual server running on the Xen hypervisor. It is powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2680 v2 Ivy Bridge processor running at 2.8 GHz, delivering 16 vCPUs across 8 physical cores with dedicated allocation and hyper-threading enabled. Memory capacity is fixed at 30.0 GB, representing an allocation of 1.88 GB per vCPU. The instance bundles 320 GB of local SSD storage, includes a baseline network throughput of 2 Gbps, and contains no hardware GPU accelerators.

Benchmark data reflects the legacy architecture of the E5-2680 v2 CPU. Single-threaded metrics are subdued, shown by a poor Geekbench single-core score of 709.0 and weak stress-ng single-core performance of 1274.28. In contrast, multi-threaded tasks demonstrate steady mid-tier capability, achieving a multi-core Geekbench score of 4594.0, a PassMark CPU score of 13469.43, and 13361.13 in multi-core stress-ng tests. Memory subsystems achieve 88.18 GB/s in large-block read operations and 46.45 GB/s in large-block write operations, with static web serving maintaining throughput of 10.85 GB/s.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance delivers moderate multi-threaded compute density accompanied by bundled local SSD capacity, avoiding separate attached block storage fees for ephemeral data. However, the lack of modern instruction sets like AVX-512 restricts vector calculation throughput and large-scale model inference, where 7B prompt processing drops to 14.88 tokens per second. The c3.4xlarge is technically suited for legacy multi-threaded computational jobs, software compilation pipelines, static web serving pools, and batch processing where predictable thread counts and local scratch storage are prioritized over cutting-edge single-core speed.
description: Amazon Web Services c3.4xlarge is a compute-optimized instance driven by an Intel Xeon E5-2680 v2 processor running at 2.8 GHz. It delivers 16 vCPUs across 8 physical cores, 30.0 GB of system memory, 320 GB of integrated local SSD storage, and a 2 Gbps baseline network interface on the Xen hypervisor. Performance evaluations show low single-threaded efficiency alongside stable mid-range multi-core throughput, supported by a PassMark CPU score of 13469.43 and multi-core stress-ng score of 13361.13. Bundled solid-state storage offers fast local I/O for scratch disks without external volume overhead, though architectural limitations such as the absence of AVX-512 reduce effectiveness on modern machine learning and vector tasks. The c3.4xlarge functions effectively for legacy multi-threaded workloads, distributed software compilation, static web serving clusters, and batch data processing pipelines requiring dedicated core allocations.
